[Bug]: MiMo-V2.5 chat template is auto-detected as string, reordering multimodal content

## Bug

The official `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5` chat template expects structured OpenAI content, but vLLM auto-detects it as `string`.

The template passes `message.content` into a macro:

```jinja
{% macro render_content(message_content) %}
  {% for content in message_content %}
    ...
  {% endfor %}
{% endmacro %}

{{ render_content(message.content) }}
```

vLLM currently detects only loops directly over `message.content`, or loops over a variable literally named `content`. It therefore misses the macro parameter `message_content`:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/4af586e185b028acf08312a4dee381b5998a137e/vllm/renderers/hf.py#L398-L449

## Impact

For OpenAI content ordered as:

```text
text "A" -> image -> text "B"
```

vLLM's default `string` path (`interleave_mm_strings=False`) moves the image placeholder to the front:

```text
<image-placeholder>\nA\nB
```

The official template should render:

```text
A<image-placeholder>B
```

Using the following option works around the issue:

```text
--chat-template-content-format openai
```

## Expected fix

Auto detection should follow `message.content` through macro arguments instead of depending on the macro parameter name. Please also add a MiMo-V2.5 regression test using `text -> image -> text`, verifying that `auto` matches explicit `openai`.

Related: #49042 fixed a similar case for the Rust frontend when the macro parameter is literally named `content`; MiMo uses `message_content`.

Tested against vLLM `main` at `4af586e185b028acf08312a4dee381b5998a137e` and MiMo-V2.5 revision `63651580ca774f8504f676040460aed3e1244ac1`.

[Bug]: CLI drops explicit empty prompts and zero token limits

### Your current environment

Reproduced with the official `vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v0.28.0-arm64` image on Linux/aarch64 in Docker. The chat/completion CLI module is byte-identical to current main `58ad1f3` (SHA256 `02672c18867aff6215db5161b5704f0864e1117d2ed56b1949633d2456ccc695`). The server uses SmolLM2-135M-Instruct on CPU with a deterministic 16-token default.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The `chat` and `complete` commands use truthiness to decide whether `--quick` and `--max-tokens` were supplied. This confuses explicit empty/zero values with omitted arguments.

Against a running server at `http://127.0.0.1:8143/v1`:

```bash
vllm complete --url http://127.0.0.1:8143/v1 --api-key EMPTY --model-name smollm2-e2e --quick Hello --max-tokens 0 --stats
vllm chat --url http://127.0.0.1:8143/v1 --api-key EMPTY --model-name smollm2-e2e --quick ''
vllm complete --url http://127.0.0.1:8143/v1 --api-key EMPTY --model-name smollm2-e2e --quick ''
```

The first command silently omits `max_tokens` and generates 16 tokens. Sending `max_tokens=0` directly to this server returns its normal 400 validation error, which the CLI should preserve. Both empty quick prompts enter interactive mode, consuming stdin or doing no request on EOF instead of submitting the explicit prompt once.

The fix should distinguish `None` from explicit values in both commands. It should not relax the server's token/prompt validation. An empty chat user message is accepted by this server; an empty completion prompt is rejected with 400.

I reproduced all three failures with native CLI processes and actual CPU inference, with six passing controls for omitted/nonempty arguments, positive/negative token limits and interactive mode. I have a small patch with regression coverage and am preparing the PR.

### Before submitting a new issue...

Checked existing issues and PRs for empty quick prompts, `CompleteCommand` token limits and falsy CLI arguments; found no matching fix. Prepared with Codex.

Root cause found (reproduced CPU-only, no GPU needed — full chain below).

**TL;DR:** This checkpoint is a dual-format repo (it ships both HF tokenizer files and `tekken.json`/`params.json`). On such repos, transformers 5.x `AutoTokenizer` returns its native mistral-common backend (`MistralCommonBackend`) — overriding the declared `tokenizer_class: LlamaTokenizerFast` — and mistral-common deliberately does not encode special tokens appearing in text:

```python
AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("unsloth/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-2506").encode("[IMG]")
# [1, 1091, 125250, 1093]   ← literal "[", "IMG", "]" — not special token 10
```

vLLM builds `PixtralProcessor` around this tokenizer (`InputProcessingContext.get_hf_processor`), so when multimodal memory profiling feeds the text-only dummy prompt `"[IMG]"`, the processor counts 1 image placeholder in text but 0 in `input_ids`, and `_check_special_mm_tokens` raises. The underlying exception (hidden behind the `Failed to apply PixtralProcessor` wrapper) is:

```
ValueError: Mismatch in `image` token count between text and `input_ids`. Got ids=[0] and text=[1].
```

This also resolves the sibling discriminator from my report: `jiangchengchengNLP/Mistral-Small-3.2-24B-Instruct-W4A16` ships no `tekken.json`, so AutoTokenizer returns a regular fast tokenizer (which encodes `[IMG]` → id 10 correctly) and the model loads cleanly. It is a checkpoint-layout interaction, not an architecture problem — any dual-format Mistral3 repo should hit this with default arguments.

**Relationship to #45289 / PR #45525:** same underlying mechanism (mistral-common not encoding special tokens from text inside an HF processor), but a different, uncovered path. #45525's fix is guarded by `is_mistral_tokenizer(tokenizer)`, which matches only vLLM's `MistralTokenizer` (`--tokenizer-mode mistral`). The tokenizer here is transformers' own `MistralCommonBackend` (arrives via plain `AutoTokenizer` under `tokenizer_mode="auto"`), for which that guard returns `False` — verified against the current PR diff. So the crash here would survive #45525 as-is. The natural fix looks like extending the same treatment (#45525 adds `_MistralCommonBackendWithSpecialTokens`, which subclasses exactly this transformers class) to the transformers-native backend in `InputProcessingContext.get_hf_processor`. Happy to open a PR for this path — coordinating with #45525's author to avoid overlap.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

> **Scope of the evidence.** The performance measurements below were collected
> with vLLM 0.24.0. The affected control flow is also present on `main` at
> [`638d6e9`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/638d6e97575c49f7e0aa128ae1e775892c92bb1c/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py):
> `Scheduler.__init__` enables deferred block freeing, `Scheduler.schedule()`
> retries allocation after preemption, and `_free_request_blocks()` defers the
> selected victim's free. This establishes that `main` contains the affected
> code path; an end-to-end performance reproduction on `main` is still pending.

## Summary

Under overlapping-batch scheduling with a consumer-capable KV connector,
`defer_block_free` intentionally delays returning a preempted request's KV
blocks until the relevant in-flight step has been processed. The
running-request allocation retry loop does not account for that delay. If its
policy-selected victim was scheduled in an unprocessed step, preempting the
victim cannot increase the free-block pool immediately, but the loop retries
and may preempt another victim.

The result is a **zero-progress preemption cascade**: a single allocation
failure can cause many requests to be preempted and recomputed even though the
scheduler already has the fence state needed to know that those frees are
deferred.

This is a performance and resource-accounting defect, not an output-correctness
or deadlock report.

## Trigger conditions

The observed cascade requires all of the following:

1. More than one batch can be in flight (`max_concurrent_batches > 1`, for
   example with asynchronous scheduling).
2. The configured KV connector has a consumer role, including the native CPU
   KV-offloading path.
3. `allocate_slots()` fails for a running request because there are
   insufficient currently available KV blocks.
4. The existing scheduling policy selects a victim whose last scheduled step
   has not yet been processed:
   `victim.last_sched_seq > processed_step_seq`.

## Expected behavior

If the policy-selected victim's block free is known to be deferred, the
scheduler should stop that allocation retry for the current scheduling pass and
wait for the relevant fence to advance. It should not scan for a different
victim, because doing so would change FCFS/PRIORITY victim-selection semantics.

## Actual behavior

The scheduler preempts the selected victim, receives no free blocks in the
current scheduling pass, retries the same failed allocation, and can repeat the
same zero-progress transition with additional victims.

### Benchmark protocol

- vLLM: 0.24.0, V1 engine
- Model: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, BF16
- GPU scope: one RTX 4090 process on a host where eight RTX 4090 devices are
  visible to `collect_env.py`
- Engine settings: `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.88 --max-model-len 8192`
- Workload: target output length 1792 tokens, concurrency 256, closed loop,
  `ignore_eos`, fixed set of 80 prompts
- Runs: 2–3 per repeated configuration; mean ± standard deviation is shown
  where it was recorded

The full environment output is supplied separately in the required
`Your current environment` field.

| Configuration | Preemptions | Recomputed tokens |
|---|---:|---:|
| No connector (recompute baseline) | 33.7 ± 0.6 | 1.12 M |
| Connector + async scheduling (affected) | **1109 ± 167** | **2.76 M** |
| Connector + async scheduling disabled (causal ablation) | 32 | 1.12 M |
| Connector + async scheduling + reclaim-aware guard | **31 ± 1** | **1.12 M** |

Additional observed diagnostics:

- Maximum victims selected in one allocation-retry loop: **132 → 4**
- Recomputed tokens before load, p50: **19184 → 1549**
- For sampled victims before the deferred free, approximately 92% of their
  blocks had `ref_cnt == 1`.
- After `_free_request_blocks()`, 100% of the sampled victim blocks still had
  `ref_cnt > 0`, and the free-pool delta was 0.
- Store-job membership among sampled victim blocks was approximately 0%, which
  rules out a store DMA pin as the explanation for the measured zero delta.

The end-to-end benchmark harness is not minimal enough to embed here. The
companion draft PR contains a deterministic CPU-only Scheduler regression test
that forces the allocation-failure path and checks the fence transition
directly. The PR will remain draft until the same end-to-end comparison has
also been run on `main`.

## Root cause

First, `defer_block_free` is enabled for overlapping batches with a consumer KV
connector:

```python
multiple_inflight_batches = self.vllm_config.max_concurrent_batches > 1
if multiple_inflight_batches and kv_transfer_config.is_kv_consumer:
    self.defer_block_free = True
```

This guard is necessary. It prevents a connector load from reusing blocks while
an in-flight GPU step may still write to them.

Second, `_free_request_blocks()` takes the deferred path when:

```python
self.defer_block_free and request.last_sched_seq > self.processed_step_seq
```

In that path, the request's blocks are removed from its ownership but are not
returned to the block pool until the associated fence is processed.

Third, the running-request allocation loop assumes that preemption can make
progress:

```python
while True:
    new_blocks = allocate_slots(request, ...)
    if new_blocks is not None:
        break
    victim = select_victim_using_existing_policy()
    _preempt_request(victim)
    # Retry allocation.
```

That assumption is false for a victim whose free is deferred. The retry sees
the same free-block capacity and may select another victim.

## Proposed fix

Before mutating the running queue or preempting the existing policy-selected
victim, evaluate the same fence predicate used by the deferred-free path:

```python
victim = select_victim_using_existing_policy()
if (
    self.defer_block_free
    and victim.last_sched_seq > self.processed_step_seq
):
    break
self._preempt_request(victim, scheduled_timestamp)
```

This is deliberately conservative:

- It does not weaken or bypass the deferred-free correctness fence.
- It does not scan for a different victim, so FCFS/PRIORITY selection semantics
  are preserved.
- It is inert when `defer_block_free` is false.
- The triggering request becomes eligible again after the relevant in-flight
  step is processed and the deferred-free fence advances.

A post-check that breaks only after a preemption fails to grow the free pool
would also stop the cascade, but it would still waste one preemption. The
pre-check avoids that known-zero-progress mutation.

## Relationship to #25538

#25538 also reports repeated preemption of a long prefill, but it does not
identify the deferred-free mechanism described here.

| | #25538 | This issue |
|---|---|---|
| Reported mechanism | Long-prefill resume/preempt cycle | Deferred-free fence × allocation retry |
| Resource accounting | Not measured | Selected victim produces a measured free-pool delta of 0 |
| Trigger | General KV pressure | Consumer KV connector + overlapping batches + unprocessed victim |
| Regression coverage | None linked | Deterministic Scheduler test in the companion PR |

The overlap is the symptom—preemption churn—not the underlying control-flow
condition.

[Feature]: Warn or auto-select the shipped score template when serving an original Qwen3-Reranker without --chat-template

### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

When an original `Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-*` checkpoint is served with the documented overrides

```
--hf-overrides '{"architectures":["Qwen3ForSequenceClassification"],"classifier_from_token":["no","yes"],"is_original_qwen3_reranker":true}'
```

but without `--chat-template examples/pooling/score/template/qwen3_reranker.jinja`, the server starts cleanly, `/rerank` and `/score` return 200, and the scores are meaningless: query and document are concatenated without the "Judge whether the Document meets the requirements..." system prompt and the `<Instruct>/<Query>/<Document>` wrapper the model was trained with.

Measured on vLLM 0.28.0 (`vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0`), Qwen3-Reranker-8B, A40, query "Türkiye'nin başkenti neresidir?" (what is the capital of Türkiye?):

| document | no template | shipped `qwen3_reranker.jinja` |
|---|---|---|
| Ankara, Türkiye Cumhuriyeti'nin başkentidir. (the correct answer) | 0.804 | 0.975 |
| Elma ve armut sonbaharda olgunlaşır. (apples and pears ripen in autumn) | 0.958 | 0.000 |
| İstanbul en kalabalık şehirdir ama başkent değildir. | 0.821 | 0.013 |
| Cumhuriyet 1923 yılında ilan edildi; başkent olarak Ankara seçildi. | 0.934 | 0.355 |

Without the template the unrelated sentence ranks first. This ran for months behind an API gateway before anyone noticed, because nothing fails. The model card, the pooling docs and `examples/pooling/score/qwen3_reranker_online.py` all mention the template, but the server itself gives no signal.

vLLM already knows it is serving an original Qwen3 reranker (`is_original_qwen3_reranker` is consumed by `Qwen3ForSequenceClassificationConfig.verify_and_update_config`) and ships the matching templates inside the image. Proposal, in order of preference:

1. When `is_original_qwen3_reranker` is true and no score template is configured, log a warning at startup that names the shipped template (`qwen3_reranker.jinja`, or `qwen3_vl_reranker.jinja` for `Qwen3VLForSequenceClassification`).
2. Optionally default the score template to the shipped file for these checkpoints, with `--chat-template` still taking precedence.

The same applies to Qwen3-VL-Reranker with `qwen3_vl_reranker.jinja`.

### Alternatives

Keep it documentation only. That is the current state and it did not prevent a silent misconfiguration in production.

### Additional context

Related: #21681 (closed as a usage question), #30550 (added `--chat-template` support for scoring). I can send a PR for the startup warning if the direction is agreed.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

[Bug]: [Kimi-K3][Hopper] Low-M TP8 KDA projection fails CUTLASS DSL compilation for sm_90a

### Your current environment

## Summary

Kimi-K3 fails to start on H100 when the low-M TP8 KDA projection-overlap path
introduced by #54697 is enabled. During CUDA-graph profiling,
`kda_skinny_gemm.run_n()` fails in the CUTLASS DSL compiler with
`NVVM_ERROR_COMPILATION` for `sm_90a`.

The failure has reproduced in two independent four-node launches. The same
deployment works on an older vLLM revision that predates #54697.

## Environment

- GPUs: 32 x NVIDIA H100 80 GB HBM3
- Topology: 4 nodes, TP8/PP4
- NVIDIA driver: 580.126.20
- CUDA reported by the driver: 13.0
- Model: `moonshotai/Kimi-K3`
- Model dtype/quantization: BF16 activations, MXFP4 weights
- vLLM image revision: `27a94d1ce4e3fc100c4732439ccec10f8246a804`
- vLLM version: `0.28.1rc1.dev337+g27a94d1ce`
- `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]`: 4.6.2, as pinned by this vLLM revision
- CUDA graphs: enabled (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`)
- Tensor parallel size: 8
- Pipeline parallel size: 4
- Maximum model length: 1024
- Maximum batched tokens: 8192
- Maximum sequences: 710
- Attention backend: `FLASHMLA`
- MoE backend: `marlin`
- FlashInfer autotuning: enabled

The local image also contains changes to pipeline-parallel communication, but
none of those changes modifies the Kimi-K3 KDA implementation,
`low_latency_gemm.py`, `kda_skinny_gemm.py`, or the CUTLASS DSL installation.

The relevant server arguments are equivalent to:


The engine subsequently reports:

```text
EngineCore failed to start.
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'NVVM backend compilation failed ...'
```

Later NCCL/TCPStore errors are teardown effects after the worker failure.

## Regression range and suspected change

The working image is based on:

```text
ac7509e2b1db40fec2f03dde1ed4e9dfdc2338c9
```

The failing image is based on:

```text
27a94d1ce4e3fc100c4732439ccec10f8246a804
```

The failing source file and dispatch path were introduced between those
revisions by:

```text
3ba9907a1db20c085be5c2d3cfbbbd6ec4a182dc
[Kimi-K3] Overlap low-M TP8 KDA projections (#54697)
```

`kda_skinny_gemm.py` was introduced by that commit and has not changed between
the failing revision and the current main revision checked during this
investigation. The PR description reports hardware validation on B300/SM100;
this failure occurs on H100/SM90a.

Kimi-K3 should start on H100. If the specialized projection kernel cannot be
compiled for SM90a, vLLM should fall back to the previous sequential GEMM path
instead of aborting engine startup.

## Workaround under test

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` causes `_enable_kda_projection_overlap()` to return
false and therefore avoids registering this specialized warmup. This is only a
diagnostic workaround because batch-invariant mode also changes unrelated
attention and collective paths.

overlap would provide a safer fallback while the compiler failure is

[Bug] fastsafetensors ParallelLoader broadcasts on group.WORLD; PP-scoped draft loads deadlock

# Draft: upstream issue — fastsafetensors loader hard-codes the WORLD process group and deadlocks PP-scoped draft loads

**Repo:** vllm-project/vllm
**Title:** [Bug] fastsafetensors ParallelLoader broadcasts on group.WORLD; draft-model load under pipeline parallelism deadlocks

## What happened

Serving Kimi-K3 with speculative decoding (DSpark) under pipeline parallelism (TP8 × PP2, 2×8 B200, EFA) fails deterministically at engine init on current main. The drafter is instantiated only on the last PP stage (correct per #50514's design). Its weight load goes through `--load-format fastsafetensors`, which uses

```python
# vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py (fastsafetensors_weights_iterator)
if torch.distributed.is_initialized():
    pg = torch.distributed.group.WORLD
else:
    pg = SingleGroup()
```

and then broadcasts every tensor on that group (`fastsafetensors/frameworks/_torch.py:138/143/147`).

The 8 ranks on the last PP stage (global ranks 8-15) enter `ParallelLoader`'s per-tensor broadcast chain, while the 8 ranks on PP0 never call it — so the **first mismatched WORLD-group broadcast hangs without error** until the 600 s watchdog:

```
[rank11] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout:
WorkNCCL(SeqNum=497221, OpType=BROADCAST, NumelIn=1, NumelOut=1, Timeout(ms)=600000)
```

Python stack at the hang (from the doomed worker):

```
.../v1/executor/ray_executor_v2.py initialize_worker
   multiproc_executor.py:648 __init__
   gpu_worker.py:442 load_model
   model_runner.py:362
   speculator.py:160
   dspark/speculator.py load_draft_model
   dspark/utils.py load_dspark_model
   model_loader/__init__.py:140 get_model
   model_loader/base_loader.py load_model
```

## Why nobody hits this so far

- Target-model loads happen on **all** ranks, so WORLD-group broadcasts always pair.
- The DSpark×PP code path is brand new (#50514) and its validation used the default `--load-format auto` (plain safetensors, no broadcasts). The overlap — spec × PP × `--load-format fastsafetensors` — is unreachable shipped product today, but the Kimi-K3 recipe pins `--load-format fastsafetensors` on Blackwell for load speed, so this is on the vendor-sanctioned path.

## Suggested fix

Scope `pg` to the weight-loading *participants*, not the world. At the draft load site the natural choice is the drafter's own TP group (`get_tp_group()` or the parallel-config-sized group for the sub-engine), falling back to WORLD when the load is genuinely engine-wide. If scoping is unavailable at this layer, a defensive alternative is to refuse fastsafetensors for sub-engine (draft) loads with a clear error, and let vLLM select plain safetensors there on its own.

## Repro

- vLLM main @ e578de311 (cu130 wheel `0.26.1rc1.dev292`), Kimi-K3 MXFP4 + Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark, TP8 x PP2, 2x8 B200,
- exact serving flags: `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --distributed-executor-backend ray --load-format fastsafetensors --speculative-config '{"model":"...","num_speculative_tokens":7,"method":"dspark",...}'` plus #50514 applied (spec under PP).
- With `LOAD_FORMAT` flipped to `auto` the same boot proceeds past draft loading (falsification of the causal chain).

Based on `loggers.py`, the `deferred` metric is `num_skipped_waiting_reqs`, i.e. requests in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` waiting for the P-side KV transfer to become ready. This report is about the observed D-side behavior where requests are counted as deferred / `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` and then fail with `Timeout waiting for P side ready`. ### vLLM version From the log: ```text v0.26.1rc1.dev77+g6f91edf96 ``` ### Relevant runtime configuration From the D node log: ```text model='/modules/GLM-5.2-NVFP4' served_model_name=glm5.2-jz data_parallel_size=8 enable_expert_parallel=True all2all_backend='flashinfer_nvlink_two_sided' enable_prefix_caching=True max_num_batched_tokens=1024 speculative_config={'method': 'mtp', 'num_speculative_tokens': 3} kv_cache_dtype=fp8_e4m3 quantization=modelopt_fp4 ``` KV transfer config on D: ```text KVTransferConfig( kv_connector='MultiConnector', kv_role='kv_consumer', kv_buffer_device='cuda', kv_buffer_size=1000000000.0, kv_connector_extra_config={ 'connectors': [ { 'kv_connector': 'MooncakeConnector', 'kv_role': 'kv_consumer', 'kv_connector_extra_config': { 'mooncake_protocol': 'rdma', 'device_name': 'mlx5_0,mlx5_5,mlx5_8,mlx5_9,mlx5_10,mlx5_11,mlx5_14,mlx5_15' } }, { 'kv_connector': 'MooncakeStoreConnector', 'kv_role': 'kv_consumer', 'kv_connector_extra_config': { 'load_async': True, 'lookup_async': True, 'cache_prefix': 'glm52-nvfp4-prod' } } ] }, kv_load_failure_policy='fail' ) ``` ### Expected behavior Requests should not remain in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` until the D-side Mooncake pull times out. Once P has finished prefill, D should either be able to pull the remote KV cache, or the system should fail/abort the corresponding P/D transfer promptly with a clear reason. ### Actual behavior D-side requests are deferred while waiting for remote KV, then many requests fail with: ```text pulling kv_caches ... failed: Timeout waiting for P side ready. ``` This causes the online PD serving system to stall under traffic. ### Notes / possible confounder The same log bundle also contains earlier 404 responses due to model-name mismatch in some requests: ```text The model `-NVFP4` does not exist. ``` However, the `deferred` / `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` interpretation and the timestamp alignment with `Timeout waiting for P side ready` suggest that at least part of the failure is in the PD remote KV transfer path rather than only an HTTP routing/model-name issue. Ideally invalid or failed P-side requests should not leave D-side requests waiting for remote KV until the P-ready timeout. ### Reproduction outline 1. Start online P/D disaggregated serving with `MooncakeConnector` over RDMA. 2. Use D side as `kv_consumer` with `MultiConnector` including `MooncakeConnector` and `MooncakeStoreConnector`. 3. Run concurrent online traffic through the PD router/proxy. 4. Observe D-side scheduler/logging where requests are deferred in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`. 5. Around the same time, observe D-side Mooncake errors: ```text pulling kv_caches ... failed: Timeout waiting for P side ready. ``` ### Questions 1. What are the expected P-side state transitions that make D-side `pulling kv_caches` leave the "waiting for P side ready" state? 2. Is there an existing metric/log line on P that directly shows the transfer entered the ready state for a given request/transfer id? 3. Could failed P-side HTTP requests, client disconnects, or router errors leave a D request in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` until timeout? 4. Should Mooncake expose clearer diagnostics for why a transfer id never reached P-ready? ### Before submitting a new issue - [x] I have searched for related issues and found #50425, which may be related but does not fully cover this observed D-side timeout/deferred behavior.

query:
[Bug][KVOffload] PD Multi Tier discards parked KV after a fixed 60s, so a queued consumer recomputes

### Your current environment

vLLM `main` (nightly `5a4c8d99`), plus #52912 applied. Two instances,
prefill and decode, each running `OffloadingConnector` with
`TieringOffloadingSpec` (CPU primary + `p2p` secondary tier).

### Describe the bug

A PD Multi Tier producer discards stored KV 60 s after `submit_store` when no
`FetchMsg` has bound the `kv_request_id` yet, so a consumer whose fetch is
issued later finds nothing, burns its own 30 s load deadline, and recomputes
the prompt.

`_UNBOUND_STORE_TIMEOUT_S = 60.0` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/manager.py`)
is a fixed timer counted from store time. Nothing ties it to whether the
consumer's request still exists or is merely queued behind other work, so the
reap can fire while the request it belongs to is perfectly alive. When the
late fetch arrives, the consumer waits out `_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S = 30.0`
(`.../p2p/session/client.py`) before falling back to recompute.

This is separate from #52808 and is not addressed by #52912; that fix makes a
warm producer cascade its blocks, this is about how long those blocks survive
while the peer has not asked for them yet.

Reproduced with two vLLM instances and three curls - no router, no proxy, no
scheduler involved. The only difference between the two cases is how long the
consumer waits before fetching:

| case | consumer fetch delay | consumer leg | bytes pulled |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| control | 5 s (inside the park) | 0.30 s | 580,962,816 |
| late | 65 s (past the park) | 38.31 s | 0 |

Producer log for the late case:

```
P2P <producer-ip>:7777: unbound store kv_request_id=park-late-39 timed out
after 60s without a fetch - failing 1 job(s)
```

### Why this fires in practice

The 60 s clock does not start when prefill completes - it starts at the
producer's FIRST stored chunk. `_build_store_jobs` iterates
`scheduler_output.num_scheduled_tokens` (in-flight requests), `complete_store`
cascades each finished store job to the secondary tiers every step, and
`_reap_unbound_stores` keys off `batches[0].submitted_at`, the oldest batch,
then pops the whole `kv_request_id`.

Measured on an idle H200 with a 98 K-token producer leg: HTTP returned in
6.7 s, the first batch parked at +1 s, and with no fetch sent the reap fired
at first-park + 60 s rather than completion + 60 s (the two predictions
differ by 6 s in that setup; the log lands on the former).

So the failing condition is not decoder queueing. The real budget is
first-chunk-to-fetch < 60 s, where the fetch only happens after the remaining
prefill, the producer's HTTP return, proxy dispatch, decode admission, and
the decode scheduler's lookup/flush. The producer's own prefill spends the
budget first: 6.7 s of it idle at 98 K tokens, 13.3 s under mild concurrent
load on the same GPU. At real concurrency on long prompts the sum passes
60 s with the decoder never queueing at all. Each occurrence costs a 30 s
stall plus a full prompt recompute, which feeds back into the load that
caused the delay.

Both leg-dispatch orders lose, so this cannot be fixed by the caller:

- dispatch the legs concurrently and the fetch can arrive **before** the
  store, so demand parks and the consumer burns its 30 s deadline. This is
  what llm-d/llm-d-router#2451 fixes on the routing-proxy side, by running
  the prefill leg to completion before dispatching decode
- dispatch them sequentially, as that PR does and as the NIXL path already
  did, and the fetch can arrive **after** the 60 s reap - this issue

A post-reap fetch is also not rejected: the reap adds the id to
`_failed_req_ids`, but the fetch-bind path never consults that set (it feeds
only the consumer-side `lookup()` and dead-session teardown, despite the
reap docstring saying otherwise). The late fetch binds, finds nothing, and
parks silently until the consumer's 30 s deadline.

### Steps to reproduce

Two instances, `PF` = producer, `DE` = consumer, both with the tiering spec
and a `p2p` secondary tier.

```sh
M=<model>; ID=park-$$
PROMPT=$(awk 'BEGIN{p="unique-'$ID' ";for(i=0;i<900;i++) p=p "alpha bravo charlie delta echo ";print p}')

# producer leg: stores KV under ID, parks it (no peer has fetched yet)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'producer http=%{http_code} t=%{time_total}\n' \
  -X POST "http://$PF:8000/v1/completions" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$M\",\"prompt\":\"$PROMPT\",\"max_tokens\":1,\"temperature\":0,\"kv_transfer_params\":{\"remote_decoder\":{\"kv_request_id\":\"$ID\"}}}"

sleep 65     # 5 reproduces the working control

curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'consumer http=%{http_code} t=%{time_total}\n' \
  -X POST "http://$DE:8200/v1/completions" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"model\":\"$M\",\"prompt\":\"$PROMPT\",\"max_tokens\":4,\"temperature\":0,\"kv_transfer_params\":{\"remote_prefiller\":{\"kv_request_id\":\"$ID\",\"remote_host\":\"$PF\",\"remote_port\":7777}}}"

# watch vllm:kv_offload_load_bytes_total on the consumer across the pair
```

With `sleep 5` the consumer pulls the blocks in ~0.3 s. With `sleep 65` it
transfers nothing and returns after ~38 s.

### The NIXL path already solves this

`NixlConnector` faces the same question - how long does P hold blocks that D
has not read yet - and answers it with a renewable lease rather than a fixed
timer:

- `_kv_lease_duration` (`nixl/base_scheduler.py`), default **30 s**,
  configurable via `kv_lease_duration`
- `_heartbeat_interval = _kv_lease_duration // 6`, and D sends periodic
  lease-renewal heartbeats to P for every request it still intends to read
- `decoder_kv_blocks_ttl`, default 480 s, for the client-driven turn-2 case

So NIXL's nominal pin is *shorter* than the tier's 60 s, yet a queued consumer
never loses its blocks: the lease is tied to consumer liveness, and only a
consumer that has actually gone away lets it lapse. The p2p tier has no
equivalent - no renewal, no way for the consumer to signal intent, and no
config knob - so it cannot distinguish "the peer is still queued" from "the
peer will never come".

### Suggested direction

Tie the parked store's lifetime to the consumer's liveness instead of a fixed
interval from store time. A few shapes that would work:

- adopt the NIXL contract: let the consumer renew the parked store the way D
  renews P's lease, so a queued request keeps its KV and a dead one releases
  it promptly
- failing that, let the consumer register intent for a `kv_request_id` before
  it is admitted, so the producer knows a peer is coming
- at minimum make the interval configurable like `kv_lease_duration` is,
  since the right value depends on the deployment's admission latency

Worth surfacing the reap as its own counter either way - today it is only a
warning line, so operators see the consumer's recompute without the producer
side that explains it.

[Performance]: DeepEP v2 (ElasticBuffer) finalize_async runs combine synchronously — the shared-expert overlap window is never used

### Report

`prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py` issues the DeepEP v2 (ElasticBuffer) combine **synchronously** at both call sites ([L171](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f179b57aa8ab6f634f508128ce1f1efadd0eb1/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py#L171), [L390](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f179b57aa8ab6f634f508128ce1f1efadd0eb1/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py#L390) pass `async_with_compute_stream=False`; the module docstring at [L45](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/41f179b57aa8ab6f634f508128ce1f1efadd0eb1/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_v2.py#L45) states both modes are synchronous).

The modular-kernel orchestration already supports overlapping **shared experts** with finalize (`finalize_async` -> shared experts on the compute stream -> receiver join, `MK_INTERNAL_OVERLAPPED`), but with a synchronous combine that window is fully occupied by the combine itself. For MoE models with a shared expert (DeepSeek-R1/V3), the shared-expert FFN therefore serializes behind the cross-node all-to-all on every MoE layer during decode.

### Prototype + evidence

We run DeepSeek-R1-671B (FP8) with `--all2all-backend deepep_v2` under full cudagraphs and prototyped a flag-gated change: combine issued with `async_with_compute_stream=True` (+ `allocate_on_comm_stream`), with `finalize_async` returning a receiver closure that waits the combine event on the compute stream (graph-replay safe). Observations on EP8 (2 nodes x 4 GPUs, TP4xDP2, GB300 / multi-node NVLink):

- **Pre-registered A/B** (4 independent server starts in ABBA order; greedy, forced 128 output tokens; steady-state ITL after warmup): **ITL p50 -8.8% @C=1 (15.71 -> 14.32 ms), -5.3% @C=24**; p99 improves similarly (no tail regression). TTFT unchanged (-0.1 ms), as expected for a decode-only change (negative control).
- **Correctness**: greedy outputs bit-identical across all four arms (same text hash). Kernel-level: 300 varied-input replays bitwise-equal vs the sync reference, both eager and inside a captured graph.
- **Serving traces**: with the flag ON, each combine kernel is overlapped by shared-expert GEMMs for ~9.7 us on average (~22% of combine busy time, consistent across ranks); with it OFF the measured overlap is exactly 0.
- **Ablation**: async combine with the event-wait placed *before* the shared-expert GEMMs (offload without overlap) shows ~0 gain - the benefit is true overlap, not stream offload. The per-layer benefit grows with EP size (~13 us/layer @EP4 -> ~18 us/layer @EP32 in isolated microbenchmarks).

### Question

Is there maintainer interest in a PR enabling this (initially env-gated, default off, disabled under DBO)? Happy to submit with a CPU contract test plus a bitwise oracle added to the DeepEP v2 GPU test, and to adapt the shape (e.g. always-on) per your guidance.

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Contract tests for DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize.finalize_async.
+
+Hermetic: fake buffer/event, single process, no GPU collectives — only
+requires deep_ep to be importable.
+
+  T1 finalize_async  -> combine is issued with async_with_compute_stream=True
+                        and the join is deferred to the receiver, which waits
+                        on the combine event (device-side) before the copy.
+  T2 DBO active      -> combine falls back to async_with_compute_stream=False;
+                        the receiver still produces the correct output.
+  T3 finalize (sync) -> combine is issued synchronously and the output is
+                        copied immediately.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.utils.import_utils import has_deep_ep_v2
+
+requires_deep_ep_v2 = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not has_deep_ep_v2(),
+    reason="Requires DeepEP v2 (ElasticBuffer)",
+)
+
+if has_deep_ep_v2():
+    import vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.prepare_finalize.deepep_v2 as _dv2
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.prepare_finalize.deepep_v2 import (
+        DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize,
+    )
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.topk_weight_and_reduce import (
+        TopKWeightAndReduceContiguous,
+    )
+
+
+class _FakeEvent:
+    def __init__(self, has_event: bool):
+        self.event = object() if has_event else None
+        self.waited = False
+
+    def current_stream_wait(self):
+        assert self.event is not None
+        self.waited = True
+
+
+class _FakeBuffer:
+    def __init__(self, out: torch.Tensor):
+        self.out = out
+        self.calls: list[dict] = []
+        self.last_event: _FakeEvent | None = None
+
+    def combine(
+        self,
+        x,
+        handle,
+        topk_weights,
+        async_with_compute_stream,
+        allocate_on_comm_stream,
+    ):
+        self.calls.append({"async_with_compute_stream": async_with_compute_stream})
+        # DeepEP returns a completion event only for an async combine.
+        self.last_event = _FakeEvent(has_event=async_with_compute_stream)
+        return self.out, None, self.last_event
+

+    pf = DeepEPV2PrepareAndFinalize(

+        num_dispatchers=1,
+        dp_size=1,
+        rank_expert_offset=0,
+        num_experts=8,
+        num_topk=2,
+    )
+    pf.handles[0] = object()
+    return pf

+    weights = torch.empty(0, 2)
+    ids = torch.empty(0, 2, dtype=torch.int64)
+    fn = pf.finalize_async if do_async else pf.finalize

+    out_src = torch.full((4, 8), 7.0, dtype=torch.bfloat16)

+    dst = torch.zeros_like(out_src)

[Bug]: --headless does not load custom reasoning parser plugins

### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Relevant environment details</summary>

```text
OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (aarch64)
Python: 3.12.13
PyTorch: 2.10.0+cpu
vLLM: 0.25.1
```

The failure occurs while constructing `VllmConfig`, before workers or accelerator resources are initialized. I reproduced it dynamically with vLLM 0.25.1 and confirmed that vLLM main at commit `16cfe728d8d0bc3cd4a8397db0f392dd52a2c109` still has the same `run_headless()` ordering.

</details>

### Describe the bug

`vllm serve --headless` does not import the file passed through `--reasoning-parser-plugin` before creating the engine config. If `--reasoning-parser` names a parser registered by that plugin, headless startup fails with `KeyError`.

This affects remote/headless ranks used by multi-node data-parallel deployments. It was originally observed in vLLM Ascend issue https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/14573, but the failing path is in vLLM core and does not depend on the accelerator backend.

Create a minimal parser:

```python
# /tmp/custom_reasoning_parser.py
from vllm.reasoning import ReasoningParser, ReasoningParserManager


@ReasoningParserManager.register_module("custom_headless")
class CustomHeadlessReasoningParser(ReasoningParser):
    reasoning_start_str = "<think>"
    reasoning_end_str = "</think>"

    def extract_reasoning_streaming(self, *args, **kwargs):
        return None

    def extract_reasoning(self, model_output, request):
        return None, model_output
```

Then start a headless rank. The command does not require the DP head rank to reproduce the early failure:

```bash
timeout 60s vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
  --headless \
  --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --data-parallel-size-local 1 \
  --data-parallel-start-rank 1 \
  --data-parallel-address 127.0.0.1 \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port 29550 \
  --reasoning-parser custom_headless \
  --reasoning-parser-plugin /tmp/custom_reasoning_parser.py
```

Observed result:

```text
  File "vllm/entrypoints/cli/serve.py", line 180, in run_headless
    vllm_config = engine_args.create_engine_config(
  File "vllm/config/vllm.py", line 1484, in __post_init__
    self.reasoning_config.initialize_token_ids(self.model_config)
  File "vllm/config/reasoning.py", line 77, in initialize_token_ids
    parser_cls = ReasoningParserManager.get_reasoning_parser(
  File "vllm/reasoning/abs_reasoning_parsers.py", line 245, in get_reasoning_parser
    raise KeyError(
KeyError: "Reasoning parser 'custom_headless' not found. Available parsers: ..."
```

Expected result: the plugin is imported before engine config construction, so the headless rank proceeds to worker launch/DP handshake instead of raising `KeyError`.

The regular API server path already has the required ordering:

```python
# vllm/entrypoints/openai/api_server.py
if args.reasoning_parser_plugin and len(args.reasoning_parser_plugin) > 3:
    ReasoningParserManager.import_reasoning_parser(args.reasoning_parser_plugin)
```

`run_headless()` instead calls `AsyncEngineArgs.create_engine_config()` directly. During `VllmConfig.__post_init__`, `ReasoningConfig.initialize_token_ids()` resolves the configured parser before the plugin is imported anywhere else.

As a control, explicitly calling `ReasoningParserManager.import_reasoning_parser(plugin_path)` before `create_engine_config(headless=True)` succeeds and produces an enabled reasoning config.

A narrow fix would import `args.reasoning_parser_plugin` in `run_headless()` before `AsyncEngineArgs.create_engine_config()`. Importing it from the `StructuredOutputsConfig` validator would be broader and would reintroduce the duplicate-registration/programmatic-registration problem removed by #28749.

**Edit:** corrected the workaround value and the mechanism explanation — see follow-up below.

Root-caused this. Two layers:

1. vLLM side: the workspace is a fixed-size buffer — `VLLM_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BUFFER_SIZE` defaults to 394 MiB (`envs.py`), allocated in `_get_workspace_buffer` (`flashinfer_mla_sparse.py`) with no awareness of DCP / heads / spec-decode config.
2. FlashInfer side: the trtllm-gen MLA decode path sizes its softmax workspace independently of the actual batch — the autotune bucket cap in `_compute_mla_decode_buckets` is intentionally decoupled from `query.shape[0]` (capped at 8192). That's why a single request is enough to overflow.

**Workaround:** `VLLM_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BUFFER_SIZE=2561671168` (~2.39 GiB). Your config needs at least 1611661312 (softmax workspace) + the 8 MiB carved before it (413138944 − 404750336), possibly more after.

Working on a fix that computes the required size from engine config at init — regrow-on-demand isn't an option since the buffer address gets captured into CUDA graphs. FlashInfer's CuteDSL path already exposes a workspace sizer (with an `enable_dcp` param); trtllm-gen doesn't, so a small FlashInfer-side follow-up may be needed. PR incoming.

Follow-up with the full derivation — two corrections to my comment above: the batch term is the *real* scheduled token count (the autotune bucket cap turns out not to be involved), and the 2 GiB workaround I suggested is slightly too small for a worst-case step; corrected value below.

The overflow is the trtllm-gen softmax-stats slab, and the reported numbers pin it down byte-exactly. Whenever LSE is requested, FlashInfer's trtllm-gen launcher carves

```text
sizeof(float2) * num_qo_heads * batch_size * round_up(max_q_len, 256) + 1 MiB
```

out of the caller's workspace (`csrc/trtllm_fmha_kernel_launcher.cu`). Three things make DCP the trigger:

1. LSE is only requested when `dcp_world_size > 1` (the DCP reducer needs it), so non-DCP runs never carve this slab — that's why only DCP crashes.
2. Under DCP the decode query is all-gathered in the head dim before the kernel, so it sees `heads_per_rank * dcp_size` = 8 × 8 = **64 heads** for GLM-5.2 at TP=8/DCP=8 (instead of 8).
3. The sparse backend routes *all* scheduled tokens (prefill included, one top-k row per token) through this MQA kernel with `q_len=1`, so `batch_size` is the per-step token count, bounded by `max_num_batched_tokens=16384` — not the request count, and not the autotune bucket (the SM100 warmup never engages the tuner on this op).

The crashing step scheduled 12,288 tokens:

```text
8 * 64 * 12288 * 256 + 1 MiB = 1,611,661,312   (exactly the requested size)
413,138,944 (default) − 8,388,608 (≤0.6.14 counter carve) = 404,750,336 (exactly the available size)
```

The static 394 MiB `VLLM_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BUFFER_SIZE` default has no DCP/head/batch awareness. For your config the crash threshold is a step with **3,081 tokens** — any prompt longer than ~3K tokens kills all DCP workers, which matches "a single request".

**Corrected workaround** (sized for your exact config — TP=8, DCP=8, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, computed as 394 MiB default + worst-case slab `8*64*16384*256 + 1 MiB`):

```bash
export VLLM_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BUFFER_SIZE=2561671168
```

(~2.39 GiB per rank; shrinks proportionally if you lower `--max-num-batched-tokens`. The 2 GiB I suggested earlier is ~9.5 MB short of a full 16,384-token step — `8*64*16384*256 + 1 MiB = 2,148,532,224 > 2,147,483,648` — so a 16K-token prompt would still crash with it.)

For anyone hitting this on a different config, the general form is:

```text
required = 413,138,944                                              # current default, keep as base
         + 8 * (num_attention_heads / TP * DCP) * max_num_batched_tokens * 256
         + 1,048,576                                                # kernel guard region
```

(On FlashInfer ≤ 0.6.14 an extra 8 MiB multi-CTA-KV counter slab is carved from the same buffer before this; it is inside the preserved base above. 0.6.15+ moves that counter to its own buffer.)

Fix in #50791: the sparse MLA backend computes the workspace up front from `dcp_world_size × heads/rank × max_num_batched_tokens` (sized before cudagraph capture, since the buffer address is baked into captured graphs), keeping non-DCP allocations byte-identical to today.

Model `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8`. ### 🐛 Describe the bug ## Summary Adding the two HiSparse flags to an otherwise plain `vllm serve` of GLM-5.2 makes every completion come back as token noise, including for a six-word prompt. The first generated token matches the non-HiSparse control exactly and every token after it is wrong; on the same HiSparse server, a chain of eight `max_tokens: 1` requests reproduces the control's output exactly, so prefill is fine and decode is not. Nothing is logged: no error, no NaN, no preemption, and the boot lines report HiSparse as active. An earlier sweep of the same configuration at TP4, on the FlashInfer sparse-MLA backend, measured GSM8K 5-shot strict-match 0.0000 with HiSparse against 0.9409 without it. ## Related issues - #56889 reports the same symptom (GSM8K ~94% to 0% strict-match with `HiSparseConnector` on GLM-5.2) on a two-node DEP8 deployment with FP8 KV and P2P offloading; a commenter sees it at TP8. This issue narrows it down: a single node, TP2, BF16 KV, no offloading connector, default settings, deterministic, and confined to decode passes. Likely the same root cause; filed separately so the minimal reproduction and the exclusion list have their own tracking. - #56699 (`cudaErrorLaunchFailure` in the host-mirror path under P/D imports) and #56785 (indexer crash during piecewise capture, fixed by #56825, which is in this checkout) are different failures. ## Reproduction Model `RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8` (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, DSA sparse MLA, `index_topk` 2048), BF16 KV cache, 2x B300 275 GB, TP2; also reproduced at TP4 and TP8. Attention backend `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` and Model Runner V2 in both arms, auto-selected. The checkpoint is 417 GiB, so TP2 is the smallest that fits on 275 GB cards; `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` would fit one card but HiSparse refuses DeepSeek V4 (`vllm/v1/hisparse/layout.py`), and every other DSA checkpoint is several hundred GiB, so we have no reproduction for an 80 or 141 GB part. ``` # broken vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 \ --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":32}}' # control: the same command without those two flags vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --max-model-len 8192 # one request, identical against both curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8","prompt":"What is the capital of France?","max_tokens":32,"temperature":0}' ``` `choices[0].text` as returned, `finish_reason` `length`, 32 completion tokens in both cases: ``` observed " (, \"' .'CC\"1adad.ss))) of,,)..-1..) of-" expected " (Paris)\n\nI am an AI language model, so I don't have personal desires or wants. However, if you are referring to the integrated system of Brain" ``` Both start with the same first token, `" ("`; the second is `","` with HiSparse and `"Paris"` without. `"2 + 2 ="` behaves the same way, returning `" .,# Had,, of to S58"` against `" 5\nThe phrase \"two plus two equals five\"..."`. Repeating a request within one server returns byte-identical noise, and two separate boots of the same command return the same text, so the corruption is deterministic. We ran the two arms on different ports so both could be up at once; nothing else differs from the commands above. ### Prefill-only requests are correct on the broken server This is the one thing we found that does not reproduce. Against the broken server above, drive the same continuation one token at a time, so every token is produced by a prefill pass: ```bash M=RedHatAI/GLM-5.2-NVFP4-FP8; T='What is the capital of France?'; G= for i in $(seq 8); do P=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "$(jq -cn --arg m "$M" --arg p "$T" '{model:$m,prompt:$p,max_tokens:1,temperature:0}')" \ | jq -j '.choices[0].text'; echo X); P=${P%X} T=$T$P; G=$G$P done printf '%s' "$G" | jq -Rsa . ``` The `jq -j` and the `echo X` sentinel matter: the third token of this continuation is `")\n\n"`, and command substitution would otherwise strip those newlines and feed a different prompt into the next step. The loop prints `" (Paris)\n\nI am an AI language"`, exactly what the control returns for one `max_tokens: 8` request, while one `max_tokens: 8` request on the HiSparse server returns `" (, \"' .'C"`. We also ran the chain with a fresh `cache_salt` per request, to rule out prefix-cache hits (prefix caching is on by default here), and got the same result. Same server, same weights, same boot: right while every token comes out of a prefill pass, wrong as soon as tokens come out of a decode pass. We found no HiSparse configuration that decodes correctly; the knobs below are the ones we varied. ## What was tried On the upstream `main` checkout above, at TP2, all through `vllm serve` plus `curl`: - `--enforce-eager`, so no CUDA graph is captured at all: still noise, byte-identical to the run above. - `hisparse_config.device_buffer_size` 2048 (the minimum for this model, one `index_topk`, no LRU slack) and 32768 (the maximum the config accepts, 8x the default 4096): still noise on both, byte-identical to the default 4096. - `--no-enable-prefix-caching`: still noise, byte-identical. - MTP speculative decoding, where `device_buffer_size` then resolves to 6144: still noise, different noise. This one arm ran through the offline `LLM()` API, not `vllm serve`. From an earlier sweep on a local branch at base `b443c1cc4`, whose HiSparse and FlashInfer code paths were unmodified upstream, at TP4 and TP8 with `host_pool_gib` 256 and a 14-prompt harness: - GSM8K 5-shot strict-match 0.0000 against 0.9409 for the control, 1319/1319 questions, all needle prompts missed, and the same first-token-right pattern. - `cudagraph_mode=PIECEWISE`, no full decode graphs: still noise, byte-identical on 10 of 14 prompts. - `hisparse_config.eager_host_mirror=false`: still noise, byte-identical on 10 of 14. - Prefix caching on in one run and off in the rest: noise either way. - `--distributed-executor-backend ray`, private per-rank host pools instead of the shared mmap: still noise. - `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE` instead of the auto-selected `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`: still noise, so both sparse-MLA backends are affected. Not tested: `MultiConnector` with `NixlConnector`, because UCX needs a locked-memory limit above this account's 8 MB cap. ## Where the evidence points The split falls exactly on the prefill/decode boundary, and it is deterministic rather than a race: eager mode, piecewise graphs, non-eager host mirroring, private per-rank host pools and prefix caching on or off all produce byte-identical wrong output. Hot-buffer capacity does not change it either: at `device_buffer_size=2048` every decode step must evict a row, at 32768 it almost never does, and the output is the same to the byte, which argues against an eviction or LRU-pressure race and for a fixed error in how decode addresses the buffer. That points at the hot-buffer decode lane in `vllm/v1/hisparse/runtime.py`, where `_prepare_for_batch` sets `decode_batch` and `_resolve_residency` (`hisparse_resolve_residency`), `_swap_rows` (`hisparse_gather_compact`) and `mirror_write_target` all branch on it. We have not isolated which of those is wrong. #56158, missing host mirror writes under FULL cudagraph replay, does not cover this: `--enforce-eager` captures no graphs and still reproduces. The boot warning recommends `NixlConnector` or `MooncakeStoreConnector` instead, but `hisparse/layout.py` raises unless the host pool comes from a `HiSparseConnector`, so the configuration above is the only shape available for a single-node run, and it is the shape the e2e test uses. ## Why the e2e test does not catch this `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py` runs with `load_format="dummy"` and a shrunk config, and its only output assertion is `assert actual == expected`, comparing generations before and after a spill. A consistently wrong decode path passes that test, because both sides are wrong in the same way, and random weights give no reference for what the output should have been.
HiSparse boot lines from the broken server ``` WARNING [vllm.py:1657] HiSparse host-resident KV is configured with connector HiSparseConnector. NixlConnector (GPU-staged host imports) and MooncakeStoreConnector (shared-store offload) are the validated paths; other connectors are treated as debug/fallback paths. INFO [cuda.py:536] Using FLASHMLA_SPARSE attention backend out of potential backends: ['FLASHMLA_SPARSE', 'FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE']. INFO [runtime.py:1276] Enabled experimental HiSparse HMA hot cache: top_k=2048, device_buffer_size=4096 (4096 LRU rows), max_num_seqs=1024. INFO [layout.py:340] HiSparse HMA: 32.0 GiB host source (5974 blocks), 34.3 GiB shared GPU indexer/resident/hot pool (124898 blocks). INFO [factory.py:62] Creating v1 connector with name: HiSparseConnector and engine_id: 5e430938-373a-4ce7-969b-ce4e6e402d18 INFO: Application startup complete. ``` No traceback, CUDA error, NaN or assertion appears anywhere in either server log.
### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

Confirmed still present on current main (`79651d6085`). ### 🐛 Describe the bug The `*_once` logging helpers (`debug_once` / `info_once` / `warning_once`) are backed by `functools.lru_cache`: ```python @lru_cache def _print_warning_once(logger: Logger, msg: str, *args: Hashable) -> None: logger.warning(msg, *args, stacklevel=3) ``` Several call sites pass a **live exception object** as a lazy format argument, e.g. `Platform.import_kernels`: ```python except ImportError as e: logger.warning_once("Failed to import from vllm._C: %r", e) ``` This has two consequences: 1. **Memory leak**: the lru_cache key retains the exception forever, and through `exc.__traceback__` every frame — and every local variable — on the path that raised it. `import_kernels` runs inside `LLM.__init__` (ModelConfig → model registry inspection → model_loader import chain), so on any platform where `import vllm._C` fails, the pinned locals include the `LLM` instance under construction. The first offline `LLM` of every process becomes permanently uncollectable: `del llm` no longer shuts the engine down, and the EngineCore subprocess survives until interpreter exit. On accelerator plugins the leaked engine keeps holding the device, so creating engines back-to-back in one process (common in test suites and notebooks) fails device initialization. 2. **Broken dedup**: each exception instance is a distinct cache key, so "once" actually logs on every occurrence. At least 9 call sites pass exceptions into `*_once` today (`vllm/platforms/interface.py`, `vllm/platforms/cpu.py` ×3, `vllm/platforms/cuda.py`, `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py` ×2, `vllm/utils/flashinfer.py`, `vllm/compilation/passes/fusion/allreduce_rms_fusion.py`). Minimal repro (no accelerator needed): ```python import gc, weakref from vllm.logger import init_logger logger = init_logger("leak_demo") class Payload: # stands in for the LLM instance under construction pass def raise_and_log(): payload = Payload() try: raise ValueError("boom") except ValueError as e: logger.warning_once("caught: %r", e) return weakref.ref(payload) ref = raise_and_log() gc.collect() print("payload alive:", ref() is not None) ``` Observed output: ```text payload alive: True ``` Expected: `payload alive: False` — the payload's only reference is a local of the returned frame, which should be collectable; instead it is pinned by the traceback of the cached exception. Regression window: v0.24 used plain `logger.warning(...)` in `import_kernels` (no cache, no leak); the switch to `warning_once` introduced the leak. How we found it: after upgrading a Neuron CI stack from vLLM 0.24 to 0.27, every test that creates two engines sequentially in one process began failing device initialization. A gc referrer walk from the undead `LLM` ended at the cached `ModuleNotFoundError("No module named 'vllm._C'")` held by an lru_cache key tuple. Suggested fix: sanitize `*_once` arguments in `_VllmLogger` — replace any `BaseException` with a hashable, traceback-free stand-in that preserves the `%s` / `%r` formatting of the original exception and compares by formatted text (fixing dedup at the same time). [Bug]: MiniMax-M3 fused SwiGLU MXFP8 kernel still uses the pre-#53110 block scale formula

### Your current environment

Verified against vLLM `main` commit `8fe9317f2e401aff6e13044098ac7f59e95dce97` (August 25, 2026). The target file is unchanged from commit `b26039b09fc97aa00f095a99eda503b7dad594ec`.

The affected kernel is ROCm-specific. I reproduced the quantization behavior with Triton's CPU interpreter because this environment has no accessible ROCm GPU. A hardware run on ROCm is still recommended.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

PR #53110 fixed the generic ROCm MXFP8 Triton quantizer to derive the E8M0 block scale as:

```python
ceil(log2(amax / FP8_MAX)) + 127
```

However, MiniMax-M3's fused SwiGLU-OAI + MXFP8 kernel still independently uses the old formula in `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/ops/swiglu_oai.py`:

```python
sb = floor(log2(amax)) + 127
```

This maps each block maximum to `[1, 2)` instead of using the E4M3 finite range up to 448. The function's docstring says it is identical to `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize(swiglu_oai_split(...))`, but its scale exponent differs by about eight steps from the corrected reference. Small values sharing a block with the maximum can therefore underflow to zero.

This path is used between the two GEMMs in the native ROCm MXFP8 MoE implementation (`mxfp8_native_moe.py`).

Minimal reproducer using Triton's interpreter:

```python
import torch

from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp8_utils import (
    _mxfp8_e4m3_quantize_torch,
)
from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.ops.swiglu_oai import (
    swiglu_oai_quantize_mxfp8,
)

m, inter = 3, 64
gate = torch.full((m, inter), 2.0, dtype=torch.float16)
up = torch.full((m, inter), 2**-10, dtype=torch.float16)
up[:, ::32] = 1.0
gate_up = torch.cat((gate, up), dim=-1)

# alpha=0 makes sigmoid(alpha * gate)=0.5. With gate=2 and beta=0,
# the activation is exactly `up`.
got_q, got_s = swiglu_oai_quantize_mxfp8(
    gate_up, alpha=0.0, beta=0.0, limit=None
)
ref_q, ref_s = _mxfp8_e4m3_quantize_torch(up)

print(got_s)
print(ref_s)
print(got_q[:, 1].float())
print(ref_q[:, 1].float())
```

Run with:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' TRITON_INTERPRET=1 python repro.py
```

Observed on current `main`:

```text
got_s = [[127, 127], [127, 127], [127, 127]]
ref_s = [[119, 119], [119, 119], [119, 119]]
got_q[:, 1] = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
ref_q[:, 1] = [0.25, 0.25, 0.25]
```

Expected: the fused kernel should use the same E4M3-aware E8M0 scale as `_mxfp8_e4m3_quantize_torch` and `_mxfp8_e4m3_quantize_triton`:

```python
sb = ceil(log2(amax / FP8_MAX)) + 127
```

I searched open issues/PRs for `swiglu_oai_quantize_mxfp8`, `_swiglu_oai_quant_kernel`, `swiglu MXFP8`, and the scale formula, and did not find an existing fix. This appears to be an omitted second implementation of the issue fixed by #53110.

[Bug]: malformed EXIF in an image fails the request with a 500 from `MultiModalHasher.serialize_item` ### Your current environment
Relevant versions (in place of python collect_env.py) The bug is in pure-Python hashing code and reproduces without a GPU or a model, so these are the versions that matter: ```text vLLM: v0.25.1 (docker image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1). The same unguarded call is still on main as of 22258a26bc09, the latest commit touching vllm/multimodal/hasher.py Pillow: 12.3.0 Python: 3.12 Serving: OpenAI-compatible server, Qwen VL model, images sent as base64 data URLs ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` deliberately tolerates bad EXIF: `normalize_image` wraps `ImageOps.exif_transpose` in `contextlib.suppress(Exception)`. But `MultiModalHasher.serialize_item` then calls `getexif()` on the loaded image with no guard, in both the `Image.Image` branch and the `MediaWithBytes` branch (`vllm/multimodal/hasher.py`). For a JPEG whose APP1 EXIF segment carries an invalid TIFF header, that call raises `SyntaxError: not a TIFF file (header b'…' not valid)`. `SyntaxError` is not a `ValueError`, so the request fails with HTTP 500 instead of 400. The error only surfaces on a *copy* of the image. Pillow's JPEG opener already parses the EXIF at open time (`_read_dpi_from_exif`) and swallows the failure. `getexif()` marks its cache loaded before it parses, so the opened object reports an empty EXIF. `exif_transpose` returns `image.copy()`, and the copy carries `info["exif"]` without that cache, so its first `getexif()` parses from scratch and raises. That is the object `serialize_item` hashes. Minimal repro (Pillow 12.3.0, no vLLM or model needed; it mirrors `load_bytes` followed by `serialize_item`): ```python import contextlib, io, struct from PIL import Image, ImageOps buf = io.BytesIO(); Image.new("RGB", (64, 48)).save(buf, "JPEG"); jpg = buf.getvalue() rest = jpg[2:]; rest = rest[2 + struct.unpack(">H", rest[2:4])[0]:] # drop JFIF APP0 payload = b"Exif\x00\x00XXXX\x00\x00\x00\x08" + bytes(32) # APP1 with an invalid TIFF header data = b"\xff\xd8" + b"\xff\xe1" + struct.pack(">H", len(payload) + 2) + payload + rest image = Image.open(io.BytesIO(data)) with contextlib.suppress(Exception): image = ImageOps.exif_transpose(image) # what normalize_image does image.load() image.getexif() # what serialize_item does -> raises ``` ```text Traceback (most recent call last): File "repro.py", line 14, in image.getexif() File ".../site-packages/PIL/Image.py", line 1647, in getexif self._exif.load(exif_info) File ".../site-packages/PIL/Image.py", line 4159, in load self._info = TiffImagePlugin.ImageFileDirectory_v2(self.head) ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ File ".../site-packages/PIL/TiffImagePlugin.py", line 602, in __init__ raise SyntaxError(msg) SyntaxError: not a TIFF file (header b'XXXX\x00\x00\x00\x08' not valid) ``` **Expected:** the image hashes and is served normally. It already loads, since `normalize_image` tolerated the same metadata a moment earlier. **Suggested fix, for the maintainers to decide:** guard the `ImageID` lookup in both branches of `serialize_item`. Catch the exception and fall through to hashing the pixels or `original_bytes`, matching `normalize_image`'s tolerance. If you'd rather reject such images, a 400 would at least tell clients the input is at fault; as it stands, a client that treats 5xx as transient retries the same image indefinitely. Happy to open a PR for whichever you prefer. **Impact:** in our deployment, one production image failed every attempt with this 500 and was retried until the retry budget ran out. We now re-encode images whose metadata fails a fresh parse before sending them, and we'll remove that once a release contains a fix. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] I searched existing issues and PRs (`getexif`, `not a TIFF file`, `hasher exif`) and found no match. I did not use the docs chatbot. _Disclosure: this issue was authored by Claude (Anthropic's AI assistant, via Claude Code) on behalf of @HipHoff, who reviewed and takes responsibility for it._

[Bug]: CPU platform silently falls back to UnspecifiedPlatform when zentorch import fails with non-ImportError

### Your current environment

vllm: 0.27.1+cpu
torch: 2.13.0+cpu
zentorch: 2.13.0
OS: Almalinux 9.8
CPU: AMD EPYC 9224 (Zen4, Genoa, AVX-512)
Python: 3.12.13

### 🐛 Describe the bug

On an AMD Zen4/AVX-512 CPU with zentorch installed, if import zentorch raises anything other than a bare ImportError (e.g. an OSError from a missing/incompatible shared library), cpu_platform_plugin() in vllm/platforms/__init__.py fails to fall back to CpuPlatform as intended, because it only catches ImportError:

if _is_amd_zen_cpu():
    try:
        import zentorch  # noqa: F401
        return "vllm.platforms.zen_cpu.ZenCpuPlatform"
    except ImportError:
        return "vllm.platforms.cpu.CpuPlatform"
return "vllm.platforms.cpu.CpuPlatform"

The exception then propagates out of cpu_platform_plugin() entirely and is silently swallowed by the bare except Exception: pass in resolve_current_platform_cls_qualname():

try:
    platform_cls_qualname = func()
    if platform_cls_qualname is not None:
        activated_plugins.append(name)
except Exception:
    pass

Result: cpu never gets added to activated_plugins, vLLM falls through to UnspecifiedPlatform, and the user sees a confusing, unrelated downstream error (RuntimeError: Failed to infer device type) with no indication that zentorch was the actual cause. The DEBUG log is actively misleading here too, since it prints "Confirmed CPU platform is available because vLLM is built with CPU" right before silently failing on the zentorch import a few lines later.

How to reproduce:

On an AMD EPYC (Zen4, Genoa or later) machine with AVX-512
Install vLLM CPU wheel + torch==2.13.0+cpu
Install a zentorch build that is ABI-incompatible with that torch version (e.g. stable zentorch pinned to torch 2.11–2.12, while torch is 2.13.0)
Run vllm serve <any model>

Actual behavior:

DEBUG [platforms/__init__.py] Confirmed CPU platform is available because vLLM is built with CPU.
DEBUG [platforms/__init__.py] No platform detected, vLLM is running on UnspecifiedPlatform
...
RuntimeError: Failed to infer device type, please set the environment variable `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG` to turn on verbose logging to help debug the issue.

Running VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG as instructed does not surface the real cause — the zentorch exception is swallowed before it's ever logged.

Manually reproducing the underlying error:

$ python3 -c "import zentorch"
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
OSError: /path/to/site-packages/zentorch/libzentorch.so: undefined symbol: _ZNK2at10TensorBase14const_data_ptrIfLi0EEEPKT_v

Expected behavior:

Either:

cpu_platform_plugin() should catch Exception (not just ImportError) around the import zentorch block, so any failure — missing module, ABI mismatch, missing shared library — falls back to CpuPlatform as intended, and logs the real exception at warning level so the user can see it; or
at minimum, resolve_current_platform_cls_qualname() should log swallowed exceptions from each plugin at debug/warning level instead of silently pass-ing, so VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG actually surfaces the root cause as its own error message promises.

[Feature][Frontend] Add per-request timing metrics to the Responses API

## Summary

Extend the response-body per-request timing metrics introduced by #46768 to the `/v1/responses` endpoint, for both streaming and non-streaming requests.

## Motivation

Per-request timing data is useful for request-level billing, SLA attribution, and latency debugging. vLLM already exposes this data in the response body for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/completions`, but callers using `/v1/responses` cannot receive the same information.

## Existing behavior

With `--enable-per-request-metrics`, supported Chat Completions and Completions responses can include:

- `time_to_first_token_ms`
- `generation_time_ms`
- `queue_time_ms`
- `mean_itl_ms`
- `tokens_per_second`

The Responses API currently returns token usage but does not expose the corresponding response-body `metrics` object.

## Proposed behavior

Reuse the existing `PerRequestTimingMetrics` representation and metric-building logic for `/v1/responses`.

Example:

```json
{
  "id": "resp_...",
  "object": "response",
  "status": "completed",
  "usage": {
    "input_tokens": 42,
    "output_tokens": 128,
    "total_tokens": 170
  },
  "metrics": {
    "time_to_first_token_ms": 85.2,
    "generation_time_ms": 1240.5,
    "queue_time_ms": 12.3,
    "mean_itl_ms": 9.1,
    "tokens_per_second": 103.2
  }
}
```

Requirements:

- Preserve the enablement and calculation semantics established by #46768.
- Support non-streaming Responses.
- For streaming, include final metrics in the terminal response event rather than introducing a separate metrics-only event.
- Preserve current behavior when per-request metrics are disabled.
- Reuse the existing engine timing source rather than recomputing timing in the Responses serializer.
- Add protocol, serving, streaming, and documentation coverage.

## Non-goals

- Reasoning-versus-visible-output timing breakdown. That requires additional token classification and phase timing and will be tracked separately.
- Changes to the Prometheus metrics endpoint.
- HTTP response-header metrics.

## Why this is not a duplicate

- #40076 was implemented by #46768, whose endpoint scope is Chat Completions and Completions.
- #42198 proposes HTTP response headers and does not provide completed streaming metrics in the response body.
- #36383 is an older draft scoped to Chat Completions and Completions.

## Related work

- #40076
- #46768
- #42198
- #36383

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched existing issues and pull requests for Responses API per-request metrics.

query:
[Bug]: CPU offload cannot pin regions of 512 GiB or more (single cudaHostRegister call)

### Your current environment

GLM-5.2 on 4×H200 NVL, TP4/DCP4, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`, vLLM `0.26.1rc1.dev255+g5e35a6f4f`, with CPU offload:

```
--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"block_size":256,"cpu_bytes_to_use":600000000000}}'
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`pin_mmap_region` registers the whole offload region with one `cudaHostRegister` call ([`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py:136`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py#L136)). A single registration of 512 GiB or more fails with `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` regardless of free memory, so any `cpu_bytes_to_use` at or above ~550e9 never gets pinned.

Bracketed with a standalone script (mmap in `/dev/shm` + `posix_fallocate` + `cudaHostRegister`), one process, 1.3 TB host RAM free, no model loaded:

| region size | result |
|---|---|
| 20 / 300 / 400 / 500 GB | success, ~0.1 s per GB |
| 549.0e9 (511.29 GiB) | success, 55.3 s |
| 549.7e9 (511.96 GiB) | success, 55.4 s |
| 549.9e9 (512.15 GiB) | **fails, code=2** |
| 551e9 / 600e9 | fails, code=2 |

So the ceiling is 512 GiB = 549,755,813,888 bytes per call. Rank count is irrelevant — one process reproduces it with 809 GB still available. I could not find this documented; NVIDIA forum reports mention other, lower ceilings in other setups (DAX-mapped memory, older drivers), so treating any single large registration as safe looks wrong in general.

This became reachable with #50094: before it each rank pinned its own `cpu_bytes_to_use / world_size` buffer (150 GB here) through torch's pinned allocator, all far below the ceiling; after it one shared region is registered in full by every rank.

Until #50070 lands, the failure is also mis-reported: the failed registration latches an error that the next kernel launch picks up, so the engine dies in `warm_v1_block_table_kernels` with `AcceleratorError: CUDA error: out of memory` on a 64-byte `torch.arange` while GiBs are free.

Workaround: keep `cpu_bytes_to_use` under 512 GiB.

[Bug]: OverflowError crash in `prompt_logprobs` decode path on PD-disaggregated (external KV connector) setup ### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py ```text - vllm: 0.23.0 (reproducible on main) - Platform: Ascend NPU (PD disagg with external KV connector) - Python: 3.12 ``` ### 🐛 Describe the bug
## 🐛 Describe the bug In a PD-disaggregated setup, sending a request with `prompt_logprobs` to the decode engine crashes the engine with `OverflowError: out of range integral type conversion attempted`. ### Root cause `prompt_logprobs` needs per-position logits, which come from running the prompt forward. But when an external KV connector (Mooncake/NIXL/LMCache) pre-fills the prompt KV, `num_computed_tokens` is advanced to `prompt_len`, so the engine skips the prompt forward and has no logits. In `_get_prompt_logprobs_dict` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py`), the last-chunk branch ships the logprobs tensor *before* checking whether there's anything to fill: ```python else: num_logits = num_remaining_tokens # 0 (or -1) because num_computed >= N-1 completed_prefill_reqs.append(req_id) prompt_logprobs_dict[req_id] = logprobs_tensors # ships the tensor if num_logits <= 0: continue # skips the copy_ that would fill it ``` The tensor is created by `LogprobsTensors.empty_cpu` with `torch.empty(dtype=torch.int32)` (uninitialized). Since the request is remote-prefilled, this is the first and only entry, so it's shipped with no `copy_` ever run. The API server then decodes every id via `tokenizer.decode`, and a negative stale int32 overflows the `u32` conversion in the Rust tokenizer, raising `OverflowError`. The local prefix-cache path is protected because `skip_reading_prefix_cache=True` (set when `prompt_logprobs` is enabled) forces a local recompute from position 0. The external connector path does not honor this flag, so `num_computed_tokens` still jumps to `prompt_len`. ### Minimal reproduction Two vllm engines (1 prefiller, 1 decoder) + the example disagg proxy: **Prefiller:** ```bash vllm serve --port 8100 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 8192 --enforce-eager \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV1","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_port":"30000"}' ``` **Decoder:** ```bash vllm serve --port 8200 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 8192 --enforce-eager \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV1","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_port":"30100"}' ``` **Proxy** (`vllm-ascend` `examples/disaggregated_prefill_v1/load_balance_proxy_server_example.py`): ```bash python load_balance_proxy_server_example.py \ --prefiller-hosts 127.0.0.1 --prefiller-ports 8100 \ --decoder-hosts 127.0.0.1 --decoder-ports 8200 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8090 ``` **Trigger** (non-streaming — vllm rejects `stream=True` + `prompt_logprobs>0`): ```bash curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model":"", "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello, introduce yourself in Chinese"}], "max_tokens":200,"temperature":0,"prompt_logprobs":1,"stream":false}' ``` ### Observed error (decoder log) ``` ERROR [async_llm.py:704] AsyncLLM output_handler failed. File ".../vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py", line 675, in output_handler File ".../vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py", line 648, in process_outputs File ".../vllm/v1/engine/logprobs.py", line 352, in update_from_output self._update_prompt_logprobs(output.new_prompt_logprobs_tensors) File ".../vllm/v1/engine/logprobs.py", line 147, in _update_prompt_logprobs else convert_ids_list_to_tokens( File ".../vllm/v1/tokenizers/detokenizer_utils.py", line 100, in convert_ids_list_to_tokens token_str = tokenizer.decode([token_id]) File ".../vllm/v1/tokenizers/hf.py", line 86, in decode File ".../transformers/tokenization_utils_tokenizers.py", line 1032, in _decode text = self._tokenizer.decode(token_ids, skip_special_tokens=...) OverflowError: out of range integral type conversion attempted ``` The APIServer then shuts down. ### Control experiments | Setup | `prompt_logprobs` | Result | |---|---|---| | PD disagg (P+D) | no | no crash | | PD disagg (P+D) | yes | **D crashes with OverflowError** | | Single engine, no external connector | yes | no crash | So the crash requires both an external KV connector and `prompt_logprobs`. DCP/MTP/memcache are not required (reproduced without them). ### Suggested fix In `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` (main @ 5672), only ship the tensor when there's something to fill: ```diff else: # This is the last chunk of prompt tokens to return. num_logits = num_remaining_tokens completed_prefill_reqs.append(req_id) - prompt_logprobs_dict[req_id] = logprobs_tensors + if num_logits > 0: + prompt_logprobs_dict[req_id] = logprobs_tensors ``` ### Expected behavior A `prompt_logprobs` request should not crash the engine when an external KV connector pre-fills the prompt KV. With the fix above the engine no longer ships an unfilled logprobs tensor; a companion proxy-side change (to be filed against vllm-ascend) returns real prompt_logprobs by harvesting them from the prefiller. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
